column1: # Reordered 2026-09-09 after a13dh0 measured the draft lm_head at 9.64 ms of a 34.62 ms step.
# All seven draft-head knobs run first: they tune the largest component this campaign has
# found, and a 20% gain on a 10 ms term is ~8% end to end - more than anything else reachable.
a5g32
a5g64
a12dch
a17dch512
a15sdf32
# a16apply REMOVED 2026-09-09: VLLM_XPU_DRAFT_LM_HEAD_INT4_APPLY_ROWS is forwarded by the launcher but read
# nowhere in the R276 image (grep of /opt in the container: no hit), so the arm would be a clean null.
# Reordered 2026-09-09 after the depth ladder closed. The ladder established that no depth
# setting beats ~110 tok/s and that single-stream gains must come from a cheaper step, so the
# draft-pass MEASUREMENT arms run first: they size the term the remaining knobs act on, and
# decide whether those knobs can matter at all or whether ~110 is this configuration ceiling.
# Ranking levers by measured size beats ranking them by plausibility.
a13dh0
a14dh0d1
a8rc16
a8rc64
# Qwen3.5-9B W4A16 TP1 lever queue, revised 2026-09-09 after the depth/concurrency map.
# Columns: run <TAB> depth <TAB> stages <TAB> harness_env <TAB> extra_env
# All arms run serially on card 0 (non-zero cards cannot host a server on this stack).
# Tier B first: the exactness mechanism is the campaign's open question and b1sn is the
# discriminator. Depth 1 is the probe depth because it has the highest measured divergence rate
# (7/128 at 64 users, 3/64 at 32), so it is the most sensitive detector of a fix. d1 is already the
# matched baseline - same depth, same rungs, same capture - so no separate control arm is needed.
b1sn
c1cap
b3lm
b2rs
# GDN speculative-path knobs, promoted: b7all decides whether the path matters at all.
b7all
b4rec
b5conv
b6delta
# Tier A speed levers. a4d4/5/6 are promoted: depth 3 buys only 0.53% over depth 2 here, so the
# curve is already flat and deeper drafts are predicted to be pure loss. Closing that with a
# measurement is worth more than another knob sweep.
a4d4
a4d5
a4d6
a1g8
a1g32
# a2scr REMOVED: VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPEC_PERSISTENT_SCRATCH is already 1 in the live container, so the arm
# would have compared a configuration against itself - inert, not neutral.
a3tight
# d2's ladders ran with a leftover diagnostic container resident on card 0, which does not affect
# identity counts but makes their aggregate figures soft. Repeat on a genuinely quiet card.
d2r
# Capture confound: were the 32/64-user speculative rungs running captured or eager? At depth 1,
# 64 users is 128 rows against a capture ceiling of 64. If raising the ceiling changes the
# divergence rate, capture fallback is part of the story rather than the norm.
# Knobs verified present in the live speculative container and currently at these values, so each of
# these is a real change rather than a no-op. Read from mtp3-a's container-inspect, not from the
# launcher's defaults, which the strict wrapper overrides.
#   VLLM_XPU_FP16_LINEAR_ROWCHUNK=32   VLLM_XPU_LM_HEAD_CHUNK_ROWS=0
#   VLLM_XPU_MTP_SUPPRESS_BONUS_TOKEN=0  VLLM_XPU_MTP_DRAFT_EAGER=0
#   VLLM_XPU_DRAFT_LM_HEAD_INT4_CHUNK_ROWS=2048
#   VLLM_ENABLE_INDUCTOR_MAX_AUTOTUNE=0  VLLM_ENABLE_INDUCTOR_COORDINATE_DESCENT_TUNING=0
# a11lmc REMOVED 2026-09-09: VLLM_XPU_LM_HEAD_CHUNK_ROWS is forwarded by both launchers but read nowhere
# in the R276 image; the in-container check would pass and the result would be a clean null.
# Autotune is off in the strict lane, presumably for determinism. Screening it is worth doing
# precisely because the identity gates will say whether that caution is still required.
x32kr
# REMOVED as unrunnable in this lane. run-w8a16-mtp1-strict-server.sh hard-pins these with no
# ${VAR:-} escape, so passing them has no effect and the arm would abort on the in-container check:
#   a9auto    VLLM_ENABLE_INDUCTOR_MAX_AUTOTUNE=0, ..._COORDINATE_DESCENT_TUNING=0
#   a6de      VLLM_XPU_MTP_DRAFT_EAGER=0
#   a10bonus  VLLM_XPU_MTP_SUPPRESS_BONUS_TOKEN=0
# The strict lane pins determinism-relevant settings by design; autotune is one of them. Testing it
# needs a separate non-strict identity, which is a different lane and a different oracle, not a knob.
# The three eliminated candidates all perturb something upstream and generic. These target the
# GDN *speculative* path directly, which is where the divergence actually lives: it appears only
# with speculation and at every depth. All three default to 0 and the strict wrapper passes them
# through with a ${VAR:-0} escape, so they are reachable.
# Direct measurement of the draft pass's share of step cost. DRAFT_HEAD=1 (draft-only INT4 lm_head)
# is the default here and was worth +27.6% on the FP8 route; turning it off measures what the draft
# head costs on THIS route. That is the term the depth decomposition says is growing
# super-linearly, so its size matters more than any remaining knob's.
# Step-cost decomposition control: depth 1 with and without the INT4 draft head isolates the draft
# pass at the depth where it is the largest fraction of the step.
# Promoted 2026-09-09 after a13dh0 measured the draft lm_head at 9.64 ms of a 34.62 ms step. These
# tune a term that is ~28% of the step; nothing else reachable in this lane acts on anything that
# large. Values shown are the live defaults read from the running container.
# Dynamic draft depth by batch size (2026-09-10). The operating map says speculation is worth ~72% at
# one user and costs a third of aggregate throughput at 64; vLLM in this image carries
# num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size, so one server can hold both ends. dyn1 is the map's own
# crossover (deep to 8 users, depth 1 to 16, off above); dyn2 tests whether depth 2 at the top is
# cheaper than 3. Strict gates prove the one-user path is still the certified one; the ladders are the
# measurement. SPEC_SCHEDULE is JSON with no spaces because the queue column is space-split.
dyn1
# dyn2 (pre-skipped: eager under the v1 runner)
# dyn1 measured 77.6 tok/s at ONE user: vLLM's v1 runner overrides FULL_DECODE_ONLY to PIECEWISE
# under dynamic speculation, and this lane's empty splitting_ops turns PIECEWISE into NONE, so the
# whole server ran eager. The override is skipped on the v2 model runner (XPUModelRunnerV2 exists in
# R276 and captures decode graphs per K). dyn2 was pre-skipped as meaningless. First prove the v2
# runner reproduces the static depth-3 certified number, then put the schedule on it.
v2s3
v2dyn1
# v2s3: the v2 runner boots, captures graphs and is lossless (12/12) but its speculative path is 26% slower
# (82.2 vs 110.7 at one user; mtp0 64.33). Not the road. Zero-patch alternative: PIECEWISE graphs with the
# DEFAULT splitting ops (attention + the GDN core ops stay eager per layer, everything else captured). vLLM
# leaves an already-PIECEWISE mode alone under a dynamic schedule. pw3 prices that mode at static depth 3;
# pwdyn1 is the schedule on it. If pw3 is within a few % of 110.7 this is the broad-speed server with no patch.
pw3
pwdyn1
# pw3: PIECEWISE with default splitting ops costs 1.9% at one user (108.6 vs 110.7) and 1.2% at mtp0, 12/12.
# pwdynm1 = pwdyn1 on the R276 + dynamic-Mamba-allocation overlay (docker/r276-dynamic-mamba-alloc.Dockerfile);
# the patch is inert without a schedule, so mtp0 stages double as a control.
pwdynm1
# pwdynm1: overlay recovers the c64 rung to 1145/1146 (from 955/995; mtp0 1203), c32 32/32 both passes, one user 108.6.
# Variable context on the same server: the 2K-32K identity ladder with the schedule active (depth32k stage).
pwdynm1x
# Residual -5% at K=0 rungs vs plain mtp0: pwdynz is the schedule with K=0 EVERYWHERE on the same overlay and graphs.
# If its c64 matches mtp0 (~1200) the residual is the rung tail where the batch shrinks and K rises; if it matches
# pwdynm1 (~1145) it is spec-decode bookkeeping running with zero drafts. pwdynm1r is a same-boot repeat of pwdynm1.
pwdynz
pwdynm1r
# Full decode graphs per scheduled K on the v1 runner (docker/r276-dynsd-fullgraph.Dockerfile), FULL_DECODE_ONLY as
# published, schedule on. This is the lossless candidate; the piecewise route failed identity at one 4K tie site.
fgdynm1
fgdynm1x
# pwdynm1x: 17/18 exact on the 2K-32K ladder; ONE 4096-context case diverged from its same-config mtp0 oracle
# (x32k and x32kr, static full-graph, were 18/18 twice). Attribution, one factor per arm, all depth32k only:
#   pw3x      static depth 3 + PIECEWISE, base R276      -> is it the piecewise graphs?
#   pwdyn1x   schedule + PIECEWISE, base R276            -> is it the overlay?
#   pwdynm1xr repeat of pwdynm1x                         -> is it intermittent?
pw3x
pwdyn1x
pwdynm1xr
# fgdynm1: 110.67/110.73 at one user (published 110.69 recovered), 33 decode graphs captured (3 query lengths x 11 sizes),
# c8 623, c32 1092/1090, c64 1064/1150, all gates 12/12. Same-boot repeat for the promotion packet and the c64 first-pass wobble.
fgdynm1r
# Transition-rung measurement: the cold first pass of a rung where K has just dropped to 0 reads low (953-1064) against
# 1090-1150 warm. Four passes at 16/32/64 on the lossless server separate the cold-pass dip from the steady figure.
fgdynt
# Past 64 users on the scheduled server: the schedule carries K=0 forward above its last range, so c128 should track the
# no-speculation c128 figure (README "Past 64 users"). Completes the concurrency map for the published configuration.
fgdync128
